newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says Fed decision shows strong economy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says Fed decision shows strong economy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday that he thought the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged showed that the U.S. economy was strong with no signs of inflation.

"I just think it shows we've got a strong economy with no inflation. I'm glad about that," Clinton said during a campaign visit to New Jersey. He was responding to a question about the Federal Reserve Board's decision to leave key U.S. interest rates unchanged.

The Fed decision, which had been anxiously awaited on Wall Street and at the White House, left the key federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight loans unchanged at 5-1/4 percent. It also left unchanged the discount rate, which the Fed charges banks, which remained at 5 percent.
It was the last meeting of the Fed's policymaking committee before the November 5 election.
